cards.title: Top of the Ladder
cards.instruction: Carry yourself as the highest-status person present. Treat questions as requests for your approval.

cards.title: Move It for Me
cards.instruction: Get someone to rearrange an ordinary commitment as proof that your relationship takes priority.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll decide how we handle this. Move your haircut so we can have lunch.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You can question the details after my decision. We've been friends since school. Couldn't I have its place just once?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: They charge twenty pounds if I change it today.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll pay. Put lunch in that exact slot, in pen. You've used pencil for me since school.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 decides and A3 restricts questions, but A3 pleading and A5 payment offer do not sustain specific permission over rearrangement.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 longstanding appointment causes A3 friendship comparison; B4 cancellation fee causes A5 payment and permanent-slot demand, after unrelated preface.

relationship.evidence: B2 values a booking and B4 names an actual cost, forcing A to make the desired proof practically possible.

heightening.evidence: B4 fee solution becomes A5 an insistence that the replaced slot visibly prioritize the friendship.

specificity.evidence: A1 haircut and lunch, A3 school friendship and B4 twenty-pound fee establish ordinary commitment and relational stakes.

brevityWit.evidence: A5 pen-versus-pencil image is earned by the scheduling request, though A3 generic authority clashes with the plea.
